question: According to an investigation published by Euractiv1 on 3 June 2026, several specialist media outlets are organising dinners, round-table discussions and conferences in Brussels sponsored by companies and trade associations, thus giving them access to EU Commissioners, their staff and officials.

It refers to 1 102 media events between 2019 and 2025 covered by sponsorship packages costing up to EUR 85 000, as well as table placements offering lobbyists the opportunity to engage directly with European decision-makers on sensitive issues. The transparency register covers meetings, conferences or events aimed at influencing European decision-making, but excludes ad hoc or private/social gatherings. 1.

Does the Commission consider a sponsored media event, when it organises or facilitates targeted access to European decision-makers, in particular Commissioners, to constitute a lobbying activity that should be declared?
How many Commissioners, members of their staff or directors-general have taken part in such sponsored events since 2019, and have details of these meetings been made public?
What changes will the Commission propose to address this shortcoming?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.8.2026) Organising conferences, events or communication campaigns with the objective of influencing the formulation or implementation of policy or legislation, or the decision-making process of the EU institutions, are interest representation activities covered by the Interinstitutional Agreement on the Transparency Register1, pursuant to its Article 3.

Interest representatives which are registered in the Transparency Register are required to declare in their registrations those activities, as well as the related financial information, including any sponsorship received or provided.

The Commission publishes information on, and minutes of, all meetings held between Members of the Commission, their members of Cabinet or Commission staff holding management functions and interest representatives in accordance with Commission Decisions (EU) 2024/30812 and 2024/30823.

These publication rules do not apply to the participation of Members of the Commission, members of their Cabinets or Commission staff holding management functions in public events, including conferences or other public sponsored media events, since information on such occurrences is already in the public domain.

In order to ensure transparency, the Commission does however require publishing information on closed-door events, as well as on any meetings held with interest representatives in the margins of such events, pursuant to the publication rules of the above-referenced Commission Decisions.
